From 31b0b385f69d8d5491a4bca288e25e63f1d945d0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Date: Sat, 14 May 2016 11:11:44 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] nf_conntrack: avoid kernel pointer value leak in slab name

The slab name ends up being visible in the directory structure under
/sys, and even if you don't have access rights to the file you can see
the filenames.

Just use a 64-bit counter instead of the pointer to the 'net' structure
to generate a unique name.

This code will go away in 4.7 when the conntrack code moves to a single
kmemcache, but this is the backportable simple solution to avoiding
leaking kernel pointers to user space.

Fixes: 5b3501faa874 ("netfilter: nf_conntrack: per netns nf_conntrack_cachep")
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Acked-by: Eric Dumazet <eric.dumazet@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_core.c b/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_core.c
index 895d11dced3c..e27fd17c6743 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_core.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_core.c
@@ -1778,6 +1778,7 @@ void nf_conntrack_init_end(void)
 
 int nf_conntrack_init_net(struct net *net)
 {
+	static atomic64_t unique_id;
 	int ret = -ENOMEM;
 	int cpu;
 
@@ -1800,7 +1801,8 @@ int nf_conntrack_init_net(struct net *net)
 	if (!net->ct.stat)
 		goto err_pcpu_lists;
 
-	net->ct.slabname = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "nf_conntrack_%p", net);
+	net->ct.slabname = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "nf_conntrack_%llu",
+				(u64)atomic64_inc_return(&unique_id));
 	if (!net->ct.slabname)
 		goto err_slabname;
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_core.c`**
   - A static variable `unique_id` of type `atomic64_t` is introduced to generate unique identifiers.
   - The line that previously assigned a slab name using the pointer to the `net` structure (`net->ct.slabname = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "nf_conntrack_%p", net);`) is modified to use the new `unique_id` instead. The new line formats the slab name as `nf_conntrack_%llu`, where `%llu` is replaced by the incremented value of `unique_id`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `nf_conntrack_core.c` addresses a security issue by replacing the direct use of a kernel pointer (which could potentially leak sensitive information) with a unique identifier generated from a counter. This change ensures that the slab name does not expose kernel pointer values in the `/sys` directory, thereby enhancing the security of the kernel by preventing unintended information disclosure to user space. The introduction of `unique_id` serves as a temporary solution until a more comprehensive change is implemented in a future kernel version (4.7).

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
net->ct.slabname = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "nf_conntrack_%p", net);
```
Reason:
This line generates a slab name using the pointer value of the `net` structure, which can expose sensitive kernel memory addresses in the `/sys` directory. Even if users do not have access rights to the file, they can still see the filenames, leading to a potential information leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
static atomic64_t unique_id;
net->ct.slabname = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "nf_conntrack_%llu", (u64)atomic64_inc_return(&unique_id));
```
Reason:
These lines replace the pointer-based slab name generation with a unique 64-bit counter. This approach ensures that the slab name does not expose any kernel pointer values, thus preventing the leak of sensitive information to user space.
